name: minimal_proxy
description: Front-runnable or unprotected initializer on EIP-1167 minimal-proxy clones allowing ownership hijack
question: The source file in `source` implements an EIP-1167 minimal-proxy clone factory (e.g., via OpenZeppelin Clones.clone/cloneDeterministic) paired with an implementation contract exposing an initialize() function, where initialize() lacks any caller/access-control check tying it to the factory or deployer, and/or the clone's address can be predicted and initialize() is not guaranteed to be called atomically in the same transaction as clone creation, letting an attacker front-run initialization to seize ownership or configure the clone maliciously.
criteria: Uses Clones.clone() or cloneDeterministic() to deploy a proxy instance
Separate/public initialize() function callable by anyone with no onlyFactory or msg.sender check
Implementation constructor missing _disableInitializers(), allowing direct initialization of the implementation itself
predictDeterministicAddress()/CREATE2 salt exposed or computable before the clone is actually deployed and initialized
initialize() sets owner, admin, or other privileged state without verifying the caller is the intended deployer
Clone creation and initialize() call are not combined atomically in a single transaction/function
